title: Phase-controlled machine
statement: Let $I$ be a set of phases, let each phase $i\in I$ have a state set $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ and a $k$-work-tape Turing machine over the alphabet $\Gamma$, and let $q_0$ be an initial state in the disjoint union of these phase state sets. Let a rule assign to each state in phase $i$ either no phase change or a state in some phase. The resulting machine starts at $q_0$: when the rule gives a state, it moves to that state with the input head and every work head staying still, writes nothing, and emits nothing; when the rule gives no state, it performs the corresponding phase machine’s transition, with any successor state kept in the same phase.
hypotheses_covered: A state set $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ for each $i\in I$
A machine over $\Gamma$ for each phase
An initial state in the phase-tagged union
A rule assigning each phase-state either no state or a phase-tagged state
